title: Bug Hunt: Recon & Dotfile Leak
story:
[BUG HUNTING MISSION - PART 1]
During web reconnaissance, bug hunters inspect exported web roots and captured HTTP responses for accidental developer leaks: hidden dotfiles (like `.env.bak`), sensitive tokens left inside HTML comments (`<!-- ... -->`), and debug flags left enabled in configuration files.
objective:
Using ONLY Part 1 commands (`cd`, `ls -a`, `tree`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `less`, `mkdir`, `nano`):
1. Explore `~/webapp_recon/` with `tree -a` or `ls -a` to find a hidden `.env.bak` file and read its `INTERNAL_ENDPOINT=...` line with `cat`.
2. Open `~/webapp_recon/logs/http_response.txt` (~600 lines) with `less` (use `/STAGING_TOKEN` to search) to find the leaked `STAGING_TOKEN=...` inside an HTML comment.
3. Edit `~/webapp_recon/config.ini` with `nano` and change `DEBUG=true` to `DEBUG=false`.
4. Create `~/bounty_report/finding.txt` containing both the leaked `INTERNAL_ENDPOINT=...` value and `STAGING_TOKEN=...` value, then run `quest check`.
hints: Run `tree -a ~/webapp_recon` or check subdirectories with `ls -la` to spot the hidden `.env.bak` file.
Run `less ~/webapp_recon/logs/http_response.txt`, type `/STAGING_TOKEN`, and press Enter to jump to the HTML comment.

Edit `~/webapp_recon/config.ini` with `nano` so it says `DEBUG=false`, create `~/bounty_report/finding.txt` with `mkdir -p ~/bounty_report` and `nano`, paste both `INTERNAL_ENDPOINT=...` and `STAGING_TOKEN=...`, and run `quest check`.
